scenes.tts: Starch in bread and cellulose in wood are both pure glucose. So why do you digest one, and not the other? The answer is one bond, pointing one of two ways.
scenes.visual: THE WORLD (carried through the whole film): an 'assembly track', a faint horizontal GOLD guide line across the middle of the frame (x -6.2..6.2, y 0), where glucose TILES live. A tile is a rounded square 1.3 wide, white fill at 15% with a WHITE outline, the word 'glucose' (TEXT, 28) inside. Every tile carries three marks, always in the same places: a TEAL tab 'C6' on its top edge (it may flip to the bottom edge when a tile is flipped), a GOLD pin on its right edge (carbon one, the anomeric carbon) and a small WHITE port '4' on its left edge. COLOR MAP: GOLD the anomeric carbon and its bond; TEAL carbon six; BLUE alpha (a bent bond, helices, starch and glycogen, fuel); GREEN beta (a straight bond, ribbons, cellulose, fiber); RED 'cannot' marks; PURPLE enzymes. Labels 30+, full opacity, at most 5 words, at most 6 things on screen. No molecular structures anywhere: tiles, tabs, pins, chips, cartoons and computed curves only. Bond angles and helix pitch are labelled 'schematic' (TEXT, 28, bottom-right) whenever drawn. Ambient motion throughout: tiles bob gently (amplitude 0.04, period 3 s, by updater) and loose tiles drift slowly in a pale water band when one is shown. SCENE: NO fade from black. Split frame. Left half: a cartoon slice of bread (BLUE outline, 60% of frame height); right half: a cartoon wooden plank (GREEN outline, same size). On 'Starch in bread' a BLUE strand labelled 'starch' pulls out of the bread; on 'cellulose in wood' a GREEN strand labelled 'cellulose' pulls out of the plank. The bread and plank remain intact but dim to 40%. On 'both pure glucose' only the two extracted strands transform into streams of identical glucose tiles that pile along the track, the left pile and right pile visibly the same tile. On 'why do you digest one' a PURPLE cartoon gut outline (a simple curved tube) slides in under the frame centre: left tiles pour into it and break into loose glowing dots; right tiles bounce off its rim and a RED X (40) pops on them. On 'one bond' everything dims to 40% except one GOLD joint between two tiles at the centre of the track, which grows to fill a third of the frame height; on 'one of two ways' a GOLD arrow on that joint swings up, then down, then up again, and keeps swinging slowly.
scenes.narration: Starch in bread and cellulose in wood are both pure glucose. So why do you digest one, and not the other? The answer is one bond, pointing one of two ways.

scenes.visual: Do not cut away: the swinging GOLD joint stays at 25% opacity. Over it: BIOCHEMISTRYPEDIA (TEAL), the title 'Same Brick, Different Snap' (TITLE_FONT 54) and a GOLD rule. Title out in the last 0.4 s; the joint shrinks back into the track as a single loose glucose strip enters from the left.

scenes.tts: In water, a glucose chain does not stay straight. The hydroxyl on its carbon five swings around and attacks carbon one. The ring closes on its own.
scenes.visual: Centre frame, filling 60% of its height: an abstract WHITE card labelled 'glucose chain' (30), with separate badges 'C1 carbonyl' (GOLD), 'C5-OH' (TEAL-white) and 'C6' (TEAL); this is not an atom-by-atom structure. A pale BLUE water band shimmers behind it (slow sine ripple by updater). On 'does not stay straight' the card flexes gently. On 'carbon five' a short arm carrying the C5-OH badge glows and swings toward the fixed C1 carbonyl badge. On 'attacks carbon one' the OH badge, not C5 itself, touches C1; on 'The ring closes' the card snaps shut like a clasp and morphs into the standard glucose TILE of the world. The C6 badge stays outside the clasp and becomes the TEAL 'C6' tab on top; the C1 badge becomes the GOLD pin on the right edge. On 'on its own' a PURPLE enzyme chip 'enzyme' slides in, gets a RED strike-through and slides out. 'schematic' tag on.
scenes.narration: In water, a glucose chain does not stay straight. The hydroxyl on its carbon five swings around and attacks carbon one. The ring closes on its own.

scenes.tts: Carbon one becomes a new, special carbon: the anomeric carbon. Its new hydroxyl group can point to either face of the ring.
scenes.visual: The tile from s02, now centred and enlarged to 60% of frame height, bobbing. On 'Carbon one becomes' the GOLD pin on its right edge pulses and grows; on 'the anomeric carbon' a GOLD label 'anomeric carbon' (34) unrolls from it. On 'new hydroxyl group' a small GOLD flag 'OH' sprouts from the pin. On 'either face' the flag swings up above the tile's plane, then down below it, and keeps rocking slowly between the two positions.
scenes.narration: Carbon one becomes a new, special carbon: the anomeric carbon. Its new hydroxyl group can point to either face of the ring.

scenes.tts: Beta means that group sits on the same face as carbon six. Alpha means the opposite face. That is the snap to follow.
scenes.caption: β means that group sits on the same face as carbon six. α means the opposite face. That is the snap to follow.
scenes.visual: The same tile splits into two copies side by side, each 60% of frame height, both bobbing, each with its TEAL 'C6' tab on top. On 'Beta means' the right copy's GOLD flag swings up to the same side as its C6 tab, the tile outline turns GREEN and a label 'β: same face as C6' (GREEN, 32) appears under it. On 'Alpha means' the left copy's flag swings down, opposite its C6 tab, outline BLUE, label 'α: opposite face' (BLUE, 32). On 'the snap to follow' a thin double-headed GOLD arrow links the two flags and pulses until the scene ends.
scenes.narration: β means that group sits on the same face as carbon six. α means the opposite face. That is the snap to follow.

scenes.tts: While that carbon is free, the ring keeps reopening, flipping between alpha and beta. In water, about two thirds settle as beta.
scenes.visual: The pale BLUE water band returns across the lower two thirds of the frame. Six small glucose tiles drift in it (slow random walk by updater); each has a GOLD flag. On 'keeps reopening' tiles briefly loosen into strips and snap shut again at random, a few at a time. On 'flipping between' flags flip up (GREEN) or down (BLUE) on each reclosing. On 'about two thirds' a horizontal bar at the top (x -4..4) fills from a COMPUTED equilibrium: 64% GREEN labelled 'β about 2/3', 36% BLUE labelled 'α about 1/3' (30 each). Tiles keep flipping underneath while the bar holds steady.
scenes.narration: While that carbon is free, the ring keeps reopening, flipping between alpha and beta. In water, about two thirds settle as beta.

scenes.tts: Now bond that carbon to carbon four of the next glucose. Once used, the ring cannot open. The face is locked in.
scenes.visual: The water band drains away to the bottom; one tile stays at centre-left on the track. On 'Now bond that carbon' a second tile slides in from the right. On 'carbon four' the first tile's GOLD pin stretches into a GOLD bond bar that reaches the second tile's port '4' and clicks into it. On 'cannot open' the first tile tries to loosen into a strip, shudders, and stays closed. On 'locked in' a small GOLD padlock icon (not a lettered label) snaps onto the bond bar and stays there.
scenes.narration: Now bond that carbon to carbon four of the next glucose. Once used, the ring cannot open. The face is locked in.

scenes.tts: Starch and cellulose both use this one four bond. Starch makes it from the alpha face. Cellulose makes it from the beta face.
scenes.caption: Starch and cellulose both use this 1,4 bond. Starch makes it from the α face. Cellulose makes it from the β face.
scenes.visual: The two-tile pair splits into two rows that fill the frame: top row two BLUE-outlined tiles joined by a GOLD bar, chip 'starch: α-1,4' (BLUE, 32) at left; bottom row two GREEN-outlined tiles, chip 'cellulose: β-1,4' (GREEN, 32). On 'this one four bond' both rows' GOLD pins and both partner tiles' '4' ports flash together. On 'alpha face' the top row's flag on the bond swings below its tile, opposite C6. On 'beta face' the bottom row's flag swings up, same side as C6. Both rows keep bobbing.
scenes.narration: Starch and cellulose both use this 1,4 bond. Starch makes it from the α face. Cellulose makes it from the β face.

scenes.tts: Put simply, the real ring is puckered. In beta, the carbon one bond points straight across from carbon four. In alpha, it leaves at a sharp angle.
scenes.visual: Zoom on one tile per row (each 60% of frame height). Each tile now shows two arrows: a WHITE arrow entering at port '4' from the left, and the GOLD exit arrow from carbon one. On 'puckered' both tiles tilt slightly into a shallow 3-D cartoon (a bent card, not a ring drawing) and rock gently. On 'straight across' the GREEN (β) tile's GOLD exit arrow rotates until it is exactly in line with its entry arrow (180 degrees, a dotted GREEN line runs through both). On 'sharp angle' the BLUE (α) tile's exit arrow swings down to a sharp angle from its entry arrow; a BLUE angle arc appears, labelled 'schematic' (no number).
scenes.narration: Put simply, the real ring is puckered. In beta, the carbon one bond points straight across from carbon four. In alpha, it leaves at a sharp angle.

scenes.tts: Now chain glucoses together each way. Which chain runs straight? Which one bends at every glucose? Picture it first.
scenes.visual: Two empty tracks, top (BLUE, 'α-1,4') and bottom (GREEN, 'β-1,4'), each with 20 faint ghost tiles in a straight line that shimmer slowly (opacity 20-35%, sine by updater). On 'runs straight' a question card 'Straight or bending?' (TEXT, 40) drops into the centre between the tracks and stays.
scenes.narration: Now chain glucoses together each way. Which chain runs straight? Which one bends at every glucose? Picture it first.

scenes.visual: Near-silence. The question card 'Straight or bending?' stays centred. The ghost tiles keep shimmering and a thin GOLD progress ring around the card fills over the 4.5 s. Nothing else changes.

scenes.tts: Beta runs straight, like a rod through beads. Each glucose sits flipped from its neighbors, so the chain lies flat, a ribbon.
scenes.visual: The card lifts away. Bottom track: GREEN tiles drop into the ghost positions one by one from left to right, each joined to the last by a straight GOLD bar (in line, per s08). On 'like a rod' a thin GREEN rod is drawn through all their centres. On 'flipped from its neighbors' every second tile turns over (C6 tab flips from top to bottom edge), a quick 180-degree card flip, so the tabs alternate up, down, up. On 'lies flat' the row widens into a flat GREEN ribbon band behind the tiles, labelled 'flat ribbon' (GREEN, 32).
scenes.narration: Beta runs straight, like a rod through beads. Each glucose sits flipped from its neighbors, so the chain lies flat, a ribbon.

scenes.tts: Alpha bends at every joint, always the same way. So the chain winds into a helix, about six glucoses per turn in amylose, a starch.
scenes.visual: Top track: BLUE tiles add one by one, each joint kinking by the same angle from s08. On 'always the same way' the growing chain curls into a COMPUTED helix (parametric x = 0.35 t, y = 1.1 cos(2 pi t / 6), z-depth by size and opacity; tiles every one step, so 6 per turn), which rotates slowly about its long axis by updater for the rest of the scene. On 'about six glucoses' one turn is bracketed and labelled 'about 6 per turn' (BLUE, 30); 'schematic' tag for pitch and size.
scenes.narration: Alpha bends at every joint, always the same way. So the chain winds into a helix, about six glucoses per turn in amylose, a starch.

scenes.tts: Flat beta ribbons lie side by side and hydrogen bond into rigid fibers. That is cellulose, which holds plants up.
scenes.visual: The BLUE helix slides up out of frame. Three GREEN ribbons slide in and stack in the frame centre (filling 60% of its height). On 'side by side' they align; on 'hydrogen bond' short dashed GOLD lines zip between neighbouring ribbons from left to right, with one label 'hydrogen bonds' (GOLD, 30). On 'rigid fibers' the stack fuses into a GREEN bar labelled 'cellulose fibril' (32) and a cartoon plant stem (GREEN outline) grows up behind it, swaying slightly.
scenes.narration: Flat beta ribbons lie side by side and hydrogen bond into rigid fibers. That is cellulose, which holds plants up.

scenes.tts: Alpha helices cannot lie flat together that way. They pack into compact granules instead: starch in plants, glycogen in animals. Stored fuel.
scenes.visual: The fibril slides right and shrinks to a third of frame width; three BLUE rotating helices drop in on the left. On 'cannot lie flat' two helices try to lie alongside each other and slip apart (a small RED 'no fibril' chip, 30). On 'compact granules' all three coil tighter and pack into a round BLUE granule blob. On 'starch in plants' the blob is labelled 'starch granule (plant)'; on 'glycogen in animals' a second blob buds off labelled 'glycogen particle (animal)'; on 'stored fuel' both glow BLUE. Helices inside the blobs keep turning slowly.
scenes.narration: Alpha helices cannot lie flat together that way. They pack into compact granules instead: starch in plants, glycogen in animals. Stored fuel.

scenes.tts: Shape is only part of the story. Digestion needs an enzyme that fits the bond. Your amylases fit alpha one four.
scenes.caption: Shape is only part of the story. Digestion needs an enzyme that fits the bond. Your amylases fit α-1,4.
scenes.visual: Left: the BLUE starch granule; right: the GREEN cellulose fibril, both at 60% of frame height. The PURPLE gut tube from the hook returns along the bottom. On 'an enzyme that fits' a PURPLE pac-man-like cartoon 'amylase' (label 30) appears, with a notch shaped to the BLUE kinked joint. On 'Your amylases fit' it glides into the granule and snips joints in the middle of the chain (not from one end); loose tiles drop out and turn into glowing dots that flow into the gut tube.
scenes.narration: Shape is only part of the story. Digestion needs an enzyme that fits the bond. Your amylases fit α-1,4.

scenes.tts: You make no cellulase to cut the beta bonds of cellulose. A cow lives on grass because its gut microbes make cellulase for it.
scenes.caption: You make no cellulase to cut the β bonds of cellulose. A cow lives on grass because its gut microbes make cellulase for it.
scenes.visual: On 'You make no cellulase' the amylase cartoon bumps the GREEN fibril; its notch does not fit the straight GREEN joint and a RED X (40) pops: 'you: no cellulase' (RED, 30). On 'A cow' a simple cartoon cow silhouette (outline only) walks in from the right and the fibril slides into a round 'rumen' bubble in its belly, where small PURPLE microbe blobs swarm (random walk by updater), labelled 'microbes: cellulase' (PURPLE, 30). On 'make cellulase for it' the microbes nibble slowly at the fibril's edges; a few GREEN tiles float free, slowly.
scenes.narration: You make no cellulase to cut the β bonds of cellulose. A cow lives on grass because its gut microbes make cellulase for it.

scenes.tts: The brick never changes. Only the face of one bond does. For glucose joined one to four, alpha coils into fuel and beta runs straight into fiber.
scenes.caption: The brick never changes. Only the face of one bond does. For glucose joined 1 to 4, α coils into fuel and β runs straight into fiber.
scenes.visual: Back to the opening split frame: bread cartoon left, wooden plank right, one GOLD joint large at the centre between two tiles. On 'the brick never changes' the two tiles pulse together, identical. On 'face of one bond' the GOLD flag on the joint swings down (BLUE) and the left side lights; on 'alpha coils into fuel' a BLUE helix winds out of the joint toward the bread. On 'beta runs straight' the flag swings up (GREEN) and a GREEN ribbon runs straight out toward the plank. The flag keeps rocking between the two faces to the end.
scenes.narration: The brick never changes. Only the face of one bond does. For glucose joined 1 to 4, α coils into fuel and β runs straight into fiber.

scenes.visual: EndCard. LINE: 'In 1,4-linked glucose, alpha coils into fuel; beta runs straight into fiber.' The small rocking GOLD joint stays alive above the line.
